title: Public Sky — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash turns successful reach into a governance problem: scale increases both opportunity and the size of any mistake, so the network needs limits as much as access.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title composition on the Launch-Shop exterior work deck with a payload silhouette, basin map, authorization cards and hard Mojave sky arranged as one visual field.

Make MORE the visual hinge: multiple routes and requests expand outward, while physical limit marks and a restrained payload ledger keep the composition grounded in engineering rather than abstract policy.
Do not show Glass Basin, Cyrus's test, a jammed consent channel, a cold-side seal failure, a satellite loss or any Issue 3 outcome.
Set the final three rule-like caption beats with increasing typographic clarity before the issue title.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One rocket proved access was possible.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Copper Lattice proved access could spread.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More towns. More requests. More water moving through systems that no longer wait for Tethergrid.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A bigger network can make a bigger mistake.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So Public Sky has to become something harder than an alternative.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It has to know who asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It has to know the limit.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And it has to know when not to move.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. The page should enlarge the moral and engineering stakes created by Issue 2 without revealing the specific tests or decisions of Issue 3. It is a promise about limits and consent, not a synopsis.
